title: Principles of management
examples: What is the main difference between Fayol's and Taylor's ideas?
Can you give an example of 'unity of command' in a modern office?
Which theory focuses more on the worker's job tasks?

explain.say: Today we learn about management principles from two thinkers. They gave ideas on how to run a business well. We will look at Fayol's ideas first. He focused on the whole organization working together.
Fayol suggested that there should be a clear chain of command. This means everyone knows who they report to. This idea is called the scalar chain. It keeps the structure clear.
Taylor focused on improving the worker's job tasks. He believed that time and motion studies could make work much faster. This is the core of scientific management.
Another key idea is 'division of work'. This means breaking big jobs into smaller, specialized tasks. Each person does what they are best at doing.
In a modern school, the principal manages the whole school. They must plan for exams, organize teachers, and control the budget. This shows Fayol's overall view.
A common mistake is thinking that efficiency only comes from the worker. Remember that Fayol stressed the need for good overall organization too. It is a team effort.

draw.text: Mistake: Focus only on one person

faq.q: What is the main difference between Fayol and Taylor?
faq.a: Fayol looked at the management of the whole organization. Taylor focused specifically on improving the actual job tasks done by individual workers.
asks: Who focused on the whole company?
Which thinker dealt with worker efficiency?

faq.a: It means that an employee should receive orders from only one boss. Having multiple bosses can cause confusion about who to follow.
asks: What is the rule about reporting to one person?

faq.q: Can a company use both sets of principles?
faq.a: Yes, most successful companies use both. They need Fayol's structure and Taylor's efficiency improvements working together.
It is a systematic approach to finding the single best way to perform a task. It uses observation to remove guesswork from work.
asks: Is it just about working faster?
Does it mean robots do the work?

faq.q: Why is the chain of command important?
faq.a: It establishes clear lines of authority. This ensures that decisions flow logically from the top down to the workers.
asks: What happens without a clear hierarchy?

facts: Henri Fayol studied the overall structure of management.
Frederick Taylor developed scientific management techniques.
Unity of command suggests one direct superior per employee.
Division of work involves specializing tasks for efficiency.

quiz.say: A manager notices that the same worker is receiving instructions from two different supervisors. Which principle is being violated?
quiz.show: One Boss, One Set of Rules
quiz.why: Unity of Command states that an employee should only take orders from one supervisor to avoid confusion.

wrong.0: This mistake confuses the source of orders with the specialization of tasks.
wrong.1: This mistake relates to the reporting line, not the number of bosses giving orders.
wrong.2: This mistake confuses organizational structure with the method of improving work.

quiz.say: A factory owner times how long it takes to wrap a product to find the fastest method. Which management concept is he using?
quiz.why: Scientific Management uses observation and time studies to find the most efficient way to complete a specific job.

wrong.1: This mistake focuses on reporting lines, not on the physical process of the job.
wrong.2: This mistake confuses the flow of authority with the process of work improvement.
wrong.3: This mistake suggests breaking the job down, but the question asks about finding the best way to do the whole process.

quiz.say: A company divides its product creation into three separate departments: design, manufacturing, and marketing. This best demonstrates which principle?
quiz.why: Division of Work means breaking a large job into smaller, specialized tasks that different people can master.

wrong.1: This mistake mixes up the concept of power with the concept of task splitting.
wrong.2: This mistake concerns the number of bosses, not how the job itself is split up.
wrong.3: This mistake suggests the overall act of linking, whereas the principle is the act of splitting.
